fact: ITWeb Africa reports Senegal's Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital launched a programme, led by the Ministry of Public Service with UNCHK technical support through Force-N, to upskill public servants in digital tools, data, AI and cybersecurity.
system: Force-N Sénégal public servants digital skills programme

fact: Senegal's Ministry of Public Service with the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Affairs validated a National Digital Training Plan for Civil Servants at a workshop, with support from Cheikh Hamidou Kane Digital University (FORCE-N) and the Mastercard Foundation.
system: National Digital Training Plan for Civil Servants

fact: Senegal validated a national digital training plan on 10 September 2026 to train state agents, with content graded by role and covering digital tools, data, information systems, AI and cybersecurity (wearetech.africa).

Senegal's Ministry of the Civil Service held a national workshop on 10 September 2026 to validate the digital training plan for state employees, developed with the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital and UNCHK through FORCE-N, before national implementation.
system: Plan de formation au numérique des agents de l'Etat

fact: The Ministry of National Education, with other ministries and UN-CHK, gave over 3,000 teachers certificates in digital skills (C2I) and AI in a pilot phase, out of 111,000 teachers, and the minister wants it compulsory for all teachers.

The education minister announced on 30 September 2025 the launch of FORCE N, run by Universite numerique Cheikh Hamidou Kane with the Mastercard Foundation, to train 105,000 teachers in artificial intelligence.

A pilot phase in early 2026 trained 583 people from three departments (Industry and Commerce, Digital, Public Service), according to Abdou Diatta at the validation workshop, which also noted a dropout rate at examinations.
system: Plan national de formation des agents de l'Etat (pilot phase)

fact: The Public Service and Telecommunications ministries, with Force N, drew up a national training plan on digital and AI skills for state agents (categories A, B and C), validated at a workshop around 10 September 2026, with a first five-module programme ready to deploy; of 183,500 agents counted, 35,857 are flagged for priority training, and the targets are 70% exam participation, 75% pass rate and at least 80% of agents in one module.
system: Plan national de formation des agents de l'Etat

fact: FORCE-N reports that a pilot in the first quarter of 2026 enrolled 583 agents of three ministries in certified digital training, with an 88 to 92 percent pass rate among those who sat the exams and 70 percent of enrollees not sitting them.

FORCE-N reports that a national workshop in Dakar validated on 10 September 2026 the national plan for digital skills of state agents 2026-2029, which targets all 183,502 state agents by 2029 in two waves of about 73,000 and 106,000.
system: Plan national de développement des compétences numériques des agents de l'État 2026-2029

fact: We are Tech reports that the Ministries of Digital Affairs and of Civil Service discussed on 18 April 2025 creating a national e-learning platform for continuous digital-skills training of civil servants, described as being explored; no launch or number trained is given.
system: national e-learning platform for civil servants
